Build succeeds. Added a `volumeButtonControls` preference, default off:

**`ios/cmux/App/cmuxApp.swift`** — registers `volumeButtonControls: false` alongside the existing default.

**`ios/cmux/Settings/SettingsView.swift`** — new "Walkie-Talkie" section above "Speech Input" with a `Toggle` and a footnote describing the four gestures (up = start/send dictation, double-up = quick actions, down = cycle surfaces, double-down = cycle workspaces).

**`ios/cmux/Layout/WorkspaceLayoutView.swift`** — both `volumeHandler.start()` sites (initial `onAppear` and the `didBecomeActive` restart) are now gated on the flag, plus an `onChange(of: volumeButtonControls)` that starts or `stop()`s the handler so flipping the toggle takes effect immediately without a relaunch.

With it off, `VolumeButtonHandler.start()` is never called, so no `MPVolumeView` is attached, no `AVAudioSession` category is set, and no volume KVO observer runs — the buttons behave as normal system volume controls. The existing touch equivalents (long-press for quick actions, horizontal swipe to cycle surfaces, the compose bar) are untouched, so the app is fully usable with the feature disabled.

feat(ios): make volume-button walkie-talkie controls opt-in

Hijacking the hardware volume buttons is surprising by default — the
buttons stop changing volume the moment the workspace view appears. Put
it behind a `volumeButtonControls` preference that defaults to off.

- Register the default as false in cmuxApp.
- Gate both VolumeButtonHandler.start() sites (onAppear and the
  didBecomeActive restart) on the flag, and start/stop on change so the
  toggle takes effect without relaunching.
- Add a "Walkie-Talkie" section in Settings documenting the four
  gestures.

With the flag off nothing is attached: no MPVolumeView in the window, no
AVAudioSession category change, no outputVolume KVO observer. The touch
equivalents (long-press quick actions, horizontal swipe to cycle,
compose bar) are unchanged.
EOF

## What

Hijacking the hardware volume buttons is surprising as a default — the buttons stop changing volume the moment the workspace view appears. This puts the behavior behind a `volumeButtonControls` preference that **defaults to off**.

## Changes

- **`cmuxApp.swift`** — register `volumeButtonControls: false` alongside the existing `autoSubmitSpeech` default.
- **`WorkspaceLayoutView.swift`** — gate both `volumeHandler.start()` sites (initial `onAppear` and the `didBecomeActive` restart) on the flag, plus an `onChange(of:)` that starts or `stop()`s the handler so flipping the toggle takes effect immediately without a relaunch.
- **`SettingsView.swift`** — new "Walkie-Talkie" section with the toggle and a footnote describing the four gestures (up = start/send dictation, double-up = quick actions, down = cycle surfaces, double-down = cycle workspaces).

## Behavior with the flag off

Nothing is attached: no `MPVolumeView` in the window hierarchy, no `AVAudioSession` category change, no `outputVolume` KVO observer. The buttons behave as ordinary system volume controls.

The touch equivalents are untouched, so the app is fully usable with the feature disabled — long-press for quick actions, horizontal swipe to cycle surfaces, and the compose bar.

## Testing

content.text:
Review complete. Here it is:

## Overview

Puts the volume-button hijacking behind a `volumeButtonControls` preference defaulting to off. Three files, +27/−3: register the default, gate the two `start()` call sites plus an `onChange` teardown, add a Settings toggle. Scope is tight and matches the stated intent.

## Correctness

**The `onChange(of: volumeButtonControls)` never fires in practice** — `MainTabView.swift:11-24` switches on `appState.selectedTab` inside a `Group`, so selecting `.settings` gives `WorkspaceLayoutView` a new structural identity and tears it down, `@StateObject volumeHandler` included. While the user is in Settings flipping the toggle, the observing view isn't in the hierarchy.

The feature still behaves correctly, just by a different mechanism than the PR body claims: returning to Layout re-runs `onAppear`, which builds a fresh handler and gates on the new value. Disabling works because the old handler is deallocated on teardown (`NSKeyValueObservation` invalidates in its own `deinit`). So the `onChange` is harmless defensive code that would matter if `MainTabView` ever became a real `TabView` — worth keeping, but the comment overstates what it does today.

**Latent race in `start()`/`stop()`** — `VolumeButtonHandler.start()` hops to a background queue and re-attaches the KVO observer in an `asyncAfter(0.3)`. A `stop()` landing inside that window is overwritten by the pending `startObserving`, leaving the buttons hijacked with the setting off. This PR is the first code to ever call `stop()`, so it newly exposes it — but per the above, the racing path is currently unreachable. Fixing it would mean a generation counter or an `isEnabled` flag checked inside the delayed closure. Fine to defer; noting it because it becomes live the moment tab state is retained.

**`stop()` leaves the audio session active** — no `setActive(false)` and no category restore, and the system volume stays pinned at the 0.5 the handler forced. Low impact (`.ambient` mixes and honors the silent switch), and irrelevant on the common path where the flag is off from launch so nothing is ever configured.

**Existing installs silently lose the feature** on update, with no in-app hint that it moved to a toggle. That's the explicit ask, so it's correct — just be aware it's a behavior regression for anyone already using it.

## Quality & style

Follows repo conventions closely: `@AppStorage` + `register(defaults:)` mirrors `autoSubmitSpeech`, the footnote-under-toggle pattern matches the Speech Input section, and comment density fits the surrounding code. The footnote accurately describes all four gestures as wired in `wireVolumeCallbacks()`. `wireVolumeCallbacks()` still runs unconditionally, which is right — the callbacks are inert without an observer.

Minor: "Walkie-Talkie" and "Speech Input" are adjacent and related; they could be one section. Subjective, leaving as-is.

## Performance / security / tests

No performance impact — strictly less work when off (no `MPVolumeView` in the window, no session reconfiguration on every foreground). No security surface. No test target exists in the project, so nothing to add.

## Verdict

Approve. Only change worth making before merge is the `onChange` comment, which claims an immediacy the navigation structure doesn't deliver.

Merged. PR #20 squashed onto `main` as `3acd939`, branch deleted, local `main` fast-forwarded.

Summary of the round trip:
- **Committed** the three iOS files on `feat/volume-button-toggle` (left your pre-existing `.entire/.gitignore` edit unstaged — it's unrelated and still sitting in the working tree).
- **Reviewed** the diff. Everything checks out functionally; the one substantive finding was that `onChange(of: volumeButtonControls)` can't fire in the current navigation structure, since `MainTabView` switches on `selectedTab` and destroys `WorkspaceLayoutView` when you open Settings. The feature still works — the teardown deallocates the handler and `onAppear` re-gates on the way back — so I kept the `onChange` as forward-protection and corrected its comment to say what it actually does.
- Also flagged, not fixed: `VolumeButtonHandler.start()` re-attaches its KVO observer in a delayed closure that a concurrent `stop()` can't cancel, and `stop()` never deactivates the audio session or restores the pre-hijack volume. Both are unreachable on today's paths; the race becomes real if the tab ever retains its view.
- **Verified** with `xcodebuild -target cmux -sdk iphonesimulator26.5` after both commits — build succeeded each time. No test target exists in the project, so nothing was run beyond the build.
